footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. Other items, net are the gains and charges the income statement shows outside these lines (−$6.9M in 2025). From pre-tax income to net income to common: after income tax and $661K of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 5.0% to $213M in 2025. Net interest income rose 4.3% to $177M and noninterest income rose 8.6% to $36.3M; noninterest expense fell 0.3%, and the provision for credit losses was $0, versus $0.
Net income to common rose 17.4% to $63.7M, or $3.72 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 58.7% versus 61.8%. HomeTrust Bancshares returned $22.0M through dividends and buybacks.
highlights: Net income to common rose 17.4% to $63.7M.
